newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oils/fats market moving into deficit - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Oils/fats market moving into deficit - Oil World.

text.p: Global output of 17 key oils and fats in 1996/97 (October/September) will fall short of consumption by 1.16 million tonnes after the 1995/96 season saw a 200,000-tonne surplus, the Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
The independent publication pegged 1996/97 output at 97.25 million tonnes compared with 95.57 million in 1995/96, and 1996/97 consumption at 98.41 million tonnes after 95.37 million in 1995/96.
It forecast price rises over the next four to six months which it said would dampen demand in some developing countries which depended on imports.
Oils/fats stocks of 11.55 million tonnes on October 1, 1996, were forecast to fall to 10.17 million a year later.
Import activity in the 17 commodities would expand by 3.9 percent over the 1995/96 season to 29.5 million tonnes, with large rises seen in China and other countries, Oil World said.
This should offset declines in India, Iran, Indonesia, South Africa, Tunisia and Egypt.
Exports of palm and soy oils should benefit from higher import demand, along with cotton, olive and lauric oils and butter. But rape and sunflower oil exports were seen falling.
